description: Findings owned by this repository, swept from the code knowledge agent's own planning documents and verified against live code. Every entry is self-contained: it carries its own reproduction, root cause, proposed fix, and acceptance, so a builder needs no other document.

projects.summary: Open, deferred, and defective items found by reading the effort's planning documents end to end, then checking each claim against the code that shipped.

entries.title: `query_datadog_code` MCP tool never wires the real-source-file citation verifier, so MCP answers can be forwarded without the file-level integrity check the CLI enforces
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/rust/crates/cli/src/pipeline.rs` (`Pipeline::open`, `Pipeline` struct, ~lines 1315-1338) and `rust/crates/cli/src/mcp.rs` (the `query_datadog_code` tool handler, which only holds a `Pipeline`). Compare to the CLI `query` path at `pipeline.rs` lines ~1151-1153, which wires `resolve::GitSourceVerifier` via `ag.with_source_verifier(sv)` whenever `--repos` is passed.

**Symptom.** An answer returned over MCP can report a citation as `verified` based only on the chunk-text check (citable `Text` vs. `cited_text`), never against the real source file at the recorded SHA. The CLI's `-repos`/`--repos` flag is the only path that adds the stronger, file-level `git show <sha>:<path>` check.

**Reproduction.**
1. `grep -n "with_source_verifier\|GitSourceVerifier" marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/rust/crates/cli/src/pipeline.rs` — shows it only appears inside the CLI `query`/`eval` command builders, gated on a `--repos` flag.
2. `grep -n "Pipeline::open\|repos_root\|source_verifier" marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/rust/crates/cli/src/pipeline.rs` — the `Pipeline` struct (used by both the MCP server and the CLI) has no field for a repo-clone root or a verifier.
3. `grep -n "Pipeline\b" marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/rust/crates/cli/src/mcp.rs` — the MCP handler only ever constructs/holds a bare `Pipeline`, with no equivalent of `--repos`.

**Root cause.** `Pipeline::open` (`pipeline.rs` ~line 1323) takes `(out, k, model_dir)` only — no repo-clone root parameter — so the `resolve::GitSourceVerifier` that the CLI wires in a separate code path (~line 1152) is structurally unreachable from `mcp.rs`. This reproduces the exact carry-over the Go-era `plan.md` §P4 recorded ("the MCP tool still carried the docs-only chunk-text check; wire a verifier into the MCP service if a forwardable MCP face is needed") — confirmed still true after the Rust rewrite, not fixed in the port.

**Proposed fix.** Add an optional repo-clone-root parameter to `Pipeline::open` (or a builder method), thread it through the MCP server construction in `main.rs`'s `Commands::Mcp(a)` arm, and wire a `resolve::GitSourceVerifier` into the pipeline's answer path the same way the CLI does, so MCP-originated answers get the same real-file citation check before `verified=true`/forwardability is reported.

**Acceptance.** A test in `rust/crates/cli/src/mcp.rs` (or an integration test alongside `rust/crates/cli/tests/integration.rs`) that starts the MCP pipeline with a repo-clone root pointed at a fixture/clone, asks a question whose chunk text has been tampered with relative to the real file, and asserts the tool response marks that citation unverified (not just chunk-text-verified). `cargo test -p cli` green.

**Scope and risk.** Touches only `pipeline.rs`/`mcp.rs`/`main.rs` in the `cli` crate; no change to retrieval, chunking, or the corpus format. Risk: if the repo-clone root isn't reliably available in the MCP server's deployment environment (it's meant to run detached from a full multi-repo clone set), the fix needs a documented fallback (chunk-text-only, explicitly marked less-trustworthy) rather than a hard failure.

**Origin.** `datadog-code-knowledge-agent/plan.md` (P4 carry-over) — this ticket documents its live-code verification, not the plan's original text.

**Evidence.** Read `plan.md` P4 section (lines 30, 224). Ran `grep -n "with_source_verifier\|GitSourceVerifier\|repos_root\|clone" rust/crates/cli/src/pipeline.rs` and `grep -n "verify\|SourceVerifier\|verified" rust/crates/cli/src/mcp.rs`; confirmed via `find` that `rust/crates/cli/src/mcp.rs` never imports or constructs `resolve::GitSourceVerifier`.

---

entries.title: C++ chunker collapses out-of-line `Class::method` definitions to the bare method name, dropping the namespace/class qualifier that in-header declarations keep
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/rust/crates/codechunk/src/codechunk_cpp.rs`, function handling `qualified_identifier` nodes (~line 308, inside the symbol-naming logic starting ~line 302).

**Symptom.** A chunk for a `.cpp` file's out-of-line method definition (`ReturnType Namespace::Class::method(...) { ... }`) gets `Symbol`/`qual` = `method` only — losing `Namespace::Class::`. The same method's in-`.h` declaration is correctly qualified as `Ns::Class::method`. Two chunks for "the same symbol" carry inconsistent qualified names, and a query for `Class::method` may not match the out-of-line definition chunk on the qualified name.

**Reproduction.**
1. `grep -n "qualified_identifier" marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/rust/crates/codechunk/src/codechunk_cpp.rs` — shows the node type is matched and, per the surrounding comment (`/// operator_name, or a qualified_identifier (Class::method) collapsed to`), deliberately collapsed to the trailing identifier.
2. Build the chunker against a real out-of-line-defined method in a clone of `dd-trace-cpp` (`<local-clones>` if present, or any clone with `.cpp`/`.h` pairs using out-of-line definitions) and diff the emitted `symbol` field for the `.h` declaration vs. the `.cpp` definition of the same method.

**Root cause.** `codechunk_cpp.rs` ~line 308's `qualified_identifier` branch keeps only the last identifier segment instead of joining all segments with `::`. Documented in the Go-era plan.md P6a review findings as "acceptable for v1" but never fixed; the Rust port carried the same behavior forward unchanged.

**Proposed fix.** In the `qualified_identifier` match arm, walk all child identifier nodes of the qualified path and join them with `::` (mirroring how `cpp_qualify` already does enclosing-scope qualification for other cases, ~line 394) instead of returning only the final segment.

**Acceptance.** A new case in `codechunk_cpp.rs`'s unit tests (or the crate's existing `codechunk_csharp_rust_c_cpp_adversarial.rs`/`te_csharp_rust_c_cpp_adversarial.rs` fixtures) with an out-of-line `Ns::Class::method` definition, asserting the emitted `qual`/`symbol` equals `Ns::Class::method`, matching the in-header declaration's qualified name. `cargo test -p codechunk` green with no regression in the existing C++ chunk-count fidelity gate (spike-10.8's S6 baseline: cpp 1293 chunks on the real `dd-trace-cpp` clone).

**Scope and risk.** Isolated to the C++ extractor. Risk: chunk IDs (`repo|rel_path#qual`, `lib.rs` line 355) embed the qualified name, so fixing this changes IDs for every out-of-line-defined C++ chunk — any downstream cache (embcache, version intervals) keyed on the old ID needs a rebuild for C++ repos, not an in-place patch.

**Origin.** `datadog-code-knowledge-agent/plan.md` (P6a review finding #1) and `spike-10.8-tree-sitter-migration.md`.

**Evidence.** Read plan.md line 228 (P6a review findings). Ran `grep -n "qualified_identifier|namespace_identifier|scope" rust/crates/codechunk/src/codechunk_cpp.rs`, which surfaced lines 302-308 with the collapsing comment and code.

---

entries.title: Chunk ID scheme `repo|path#qual` collides on same-named overloads/constructors, so downstream ID-keyed dedup silently drops sibling chunks
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/rust/crates/codechunk/src/lib.rs`, chunk construction, `id: format!("{repo}|{rel_path}#{qual}")` at line 355.

**Symptom.** Two distinct symbols that share a qualified name in the same file — C++/Swift/Kotlin method overloads, multiple constructors/`init`s, C# overloaded members — produce identical chunk IDs. Both chunks are emitted by the chunker (extraction fidelity is unaffected), but any later stage that dedups or looks up by ID keeps only one and silently discards the other, so one overload becomes unretrievable/uncitable while looking, from the outside, like a complete corpus.

**Reproduction.**
1. `grep -n 'id: format!' marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/rust/crates/codechunk/src/lib.rs` → line 355, confirms the ID has no signature/arity component.
2. Chunk a file with two overloaded methods of the same name (e.g. a C# class with `Foo(int)` and `Foo(string)`, or a Swift type with two `init` overloads) and inspect `corpus/chunks.jsonl` for duplicate `id` values with different `text`.
3. Any code path that builds a `HashMap<id, Chunk>` (e.g. incremental-refresh orphan pruning, embcache lookups keyed by content_hash rather than id are unaffected, but any future id-keyed map is not) will keep only the last-inserted chunk per id.

**Root cause.** `lib.rs:355`'s ID formula uses only `repo`, `rel_path`, and `qual` (qualified name) — no function signature/arity discriminator — so two overloads of the same name in the same file necessarily collide. Documented as a known, unresolved cross-cutting limitation in the Go-era `plan.md` P6a review findings and carried forward unchanged into the Rust port.

**Proposed fix.** Extend the ID formula to include a signature fingerprint (e.g. parameter count/type list, or an ordinal suffix per duplicate qualname within the same file) so overloads/multiple-constructors get distinct IDs. Confirm no current consumer (embcache, retrieval index, version-interval identity) depends on the old ID format's exact shape before changing it — version-interval identity in particular is documented elsewhere as keying on qualname, not ID, so this may be lower-risk than it looks, but must be checked in `rust/crates/version/`.

**Acceptance.** A unit test in `codechunk`'s test suite with two overloaded methods of the same name in one file, asserting the two emitted chunks have distinct `id` values. Grep the full `corpus/chunks.jsonl` for duplicate `(repo, rel_path, qual)`-derived IDs before and after the fix to confirm the collision count drops to zero on at least one affected repo (e.g. `dd-trace-dotnet`, `dd-sdk-ios`, or `dd-trace-cpp`).

**Scope and risk.** Touches the chunk ID formula, which is a corpus-format change — every already-built corpus (chunks.jsonl, embcache.bin, version intervals) for repos with overloads needs a rebuild, not a patch. Check `rust/crates/version/` for any code that parses or matches on the id's `#qual` suffix before landing this, since that crate is explicitly documented to key symbol identity on qualname, not the id string, but should be re-verified rather than assumed.

**Origin.** `datadog-code-knowledge-agent/plan.md` (P6a review finding #2).

**Evidence.** Read plan.md line 228. Ran `grep -rn "id: format!" rust/crates/codechunk/src/lib.rs`, confirming line 355's formula still lacks a signature discriminator in the live Rust code.

---

entries.title: Dense-vector retrieval is an unindexed brute-force linear scan over every embedding, with no ANN structure, against a corpus that has grown past the point the plan assumed it would need one
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/rust/crates/retrieve/src/vector.rs`, function `vector_search` (lines 76-86), which does `vecs.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, v)| dot(v, q))` over the entire in-memory vector set for every query.

**Symptom.** Every query-time dense-retrieval call costs O(N) dot products against the full corpus vector set, with no approximate-nearest-neighbor index (HNSW or otherwise) anywhere in the `retrieve` crate. `corpus/embcache.bin` in the live build is 746 MB and `corpus/chunks.jsonl` is 612 MB across 22 repos (244,716+ chunks sampled) — well past the 2-repo, 1670-chunk scale the plan's "measure at P6 before adding a dependency" decision was written against.

**Reproduction.**
1. `grep -n "fn vector_search" -A 12 marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/rust/crates/retrieve/src/vector.rs` — shows the full linear scan, no index structure.
2. `find rust/crates/retrieve -name "*.rs"` — no `hnsw`/`ann`/`index` module beyond the brute-force `vector.rs` and the BM25/rank helpers.
3. `wc -l corpus/chunks.jsonl` / `ls -la corpus/embcache.bin` — confirms current corpus scale (612 MB chunks, 746 MB embcache) far exceeds the S0 spike's 2-repo test scale.

**Root cause.** No code gap per se — this is the plan's own open decision #10.6 ("Vector store at scale — brute force vs. ANN (HNSW). Measure at P6 before adding a dependency") never revisited once the corpus scaled to 22 repos. Not established whether current query latency has actually degraded to a problem; only that the decision point the plan set was never re-measured against the corpus that now exists.

**Proposed fix.** Benchmark `vector_search` end-to-end query latency against the current full corpus (representative query count, single-repo-scoped vs. unscoped-fanout) to determine whether brute-force cosine is still acceptable. If it has degraded past an acceptable bar, add an ANN index (e.g. `hnsw_rs` or similar, behind the existing `Retriever`-style interface referenced in the plan) gated behind a feature flag so exact brute-force stays available for eval-gate determinism.

**Acceptance.** A benchmark report (criterion or a simple timed harness) showing p50/p99 query latency against the live 22-repo corpus, with an explicit go/no-go verdict against a stated latency bar. If ANN is added: the offline retrieval gate (`cargo test`/`ka eval -retrieval`) must show no recall regression vs. the brute-force baseline.

**Scope and risk.** Purely additive if an ANN index is adopted behind a flag — no change to existing brute-force behavior when unused. Risk: an ANN index trades exact recall for speed, which could silently regress the eval gate's recall bar if not carefully validated; the ticket's acceptance criterion exists specifically to catch that before it ships as a default.

**Origin.** `datadog-code-knowledge-agent/plan.md` (§10, open decision #6).

**Evidence.** Read plan.md §10 item 6. Ran `grep -n "fn vector_search" -A 12 rust/crates/retrieve/src/vector.rs`; ran `find rust/crates/retrieve/src -name "*.rs"` to confirm no ANN module exists; ran `ls -la corpus/` to get current corpus size; ran a Python scan of `corpus/chunks.jsonl` confirming 22 distinct repos and 244,716+ sampled chunk rows.

---

entries.title: Serverless Lambda layer/extension versions remain fully unresolved — no internal usage data source found, all five `datadog-lambda-*` repos indexed only at `main` with no version-interval coverage
entries.feedback:
**Component.** `marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/version-sets.json`, `serverless_layers` block (the `_note` field and the five `datadog-lambda-extension`/`datadog-lambda-python`/`datadog-lambda-go`/`datadog-lambda-java`/`datadog-lambda-rb` entries, each `"status": "unresolved"`, `"deferred": true`, `"lines": []`).

**Symptom.** A support query pinned to a specific Lambda layer/extension version (the exact "which version are you on?" case the plan calls the first question on every support thread) cannot be answered with version-scoped retrieval for any serverless repo — the agent can only answer against `main` plus whatever changelog/git-show fallback exists, with no `introduced_in`/`last_seen_in` interval coverage, unlike every tracer and RUM SDK.

**Reproduction.**
1. `grep -n "serverless_layers" -A 40 marketplace-datadog/plugins/knowledge-agents/datadog-code-knowledge-agent/version-sets.json` — shows `"source": "unresolved"`, `"lines": []`, `"caveats": "no layer-version telemetry source found."` repeated for all five serverless repos.
2. Confirm no serverless repo appears with version-interval coverage: `python3 -c "import json; [print(json.loads(l).get('introduced_in')) for l in open('corpus/chunks.jsonl') if json.loads(l).get('repo','').startswith('datadog-lambda')]"` (sample-limited) shows no populated version intervals for these repos in the live corpus.

**Root cause.** Not a code defect — a data-source gap. Every version column reachable from outside the vendor records the function's own version, not the layer's. No alternative source has been found.

**Proposed fix.** Either (a) find an alternative internal usage data source for layer version (e.g. Lambda layer ARN version suffix logged somewhere in Datadog's own telemetry, or an installer/init-time ping that reports layer version), or (b) explicitly accept the git-tags-only fallback (`main` + changelog + on-demand `git show`, same model already used for a private repository) as the permanent model for serverless and update `version-sets.json`'s `status` from `unresolved` to a deliberate `git-tags-only` status (mirroring the a private repository entry) rather than leaving it as an open unresolved gap.

**Acceptance.** Either a working an internal usage source query populating real major.minor lines for at least one `datadog-lambda-*` repo (mirroring the tracer/RUM discovery pattern), or an explicit operator decision recorded in `version-sets.json` (status changed from `unresolved` to a named permanent fallback) plus updated `-version` query documentation in the subagent face reflecting that serverless queries are unscoped-by-version by design.

**Scope and risk.** Data/decision work, not a code change, unless a new an internal usage source table is found (in which case it's a version-sets.json regeneration via the existing `reselect-versions` mode). No risk to other repos' version coverage.

**Origin.** `datadog-code-knowledge-agent/plan.md` (§6.2, "Serverless layer version: STILL UNRESOLVED").

**Evidence.** Read plan.md §6 step 2 (serverless bullet). Read `version-sets.json` lines 785+ (`serverless_layers` block) confirming all five entries remain `status: unresolved`/`deferred: true` with empty `lines` arrays, unchanged since the plan's 2026-06-22 note.

---

## Findings investigated and dropped (verified already resolved or already tracked elsewhere)

- **P6a dart language support / "no bundled grammar, BLOCKED"** (plan.md P6a, P6b) — resolved. `spike-10.8-tree-sitter-migration.md` documents `UserNobody14/tree-sitter-dart` bundled at ABI-15 tip, and an `extension_type_declaration` fix landing 2026-06-23 (dd-sdk-flutter → 4926 chunks). Live corpus confirms `dd-sdk-flutter` and `dd-sdk-android`/`dd-sdk-ios` are all indexed with `status: ready` version-sets.
- **`datadog-agent` monorepo "whole tree" scale concern / missing package allowlist** (plan.md §10.5, P6c) — resolved. Live `corpus/chunks.jsonl` shows `datadog-agent` chunks scoped only to `pkg/trace` (4027), `pkg/obfuscate` (339), `pkg/remoteconfig` (218) — an allowlist is already applied, matching `version-sets.json`'s caveat text.
- **a private repository (a private repository) visibility gating** (plan.md §6.2/P6c) — resolved. Live corpus confirms all 7568 a private repository chunks are tagged `visibility: internal`; `version-sets.json` records the same.
- **browser-sdk version-tail undercount** ("re-run with version top_n≈200 to size it", plan.md §6.2) — resolved. `version-sets.json`'s `browser-sdk` entry records a resolved re-pull at `top_n=500` showing the earlier "deep tail" was a patch-level truncation artifact, not a real gap.
- **dd-trace-go v1.74 relocation / `IncludeDirs` destination-dir scoping gap** (plan.md §6, Pv carry-over) — resolved. `version-sets.json`'s `dd-trace-go` entry already includes `internal` in its `include` list, which is where the relocated files landed.
- **Swift/C# tree-sitter grammar ERROR-tolerance follow-up** (spike-10.8 §S6 resolution) — a real, still-open limitation, but explicitly logged and operator-accepted as a known limitation with a tracked follow-up in the source document itself, not a silently-dropped item; not filed as a new ticket since the document already carries it as an accepted, tracked risk rather than an unresolved defect.
- **Any Rust-rewrite-specific gap** (reranker `tau` calibration for code, pre-retrieval version-filter pruning + latency re-benchmark, memory-mapped corpus loading, CLI/MCP fuzzy `--repo`/`--version` resolution, 22-repo golden coverage expansion) — all live, explicitly tracked in the successor effort `.dat/datadog-code-agent/` (`plan.json` success criteria M9/M11/M12; `execution.json` shows M11.P1.T1 in-progress, M11.P2.T1/M11.P3.T1/M13.P1-P4 not-started). Not re-filed here per the task instructions.
